US-525 DONE (Sprint 70 / V0.29.25, 4/8) -- BUT *** UNCOMMITTED ***. READ THE NEXT PARAGRAPH BEFORE ANYTHING ELSE.

*** BL-029: A STALE .git/index.lock BLOCKS EVERY COMMIT ON THIS CHECKOUT. *** 0 bytes, created 08:26, still there 13+ min later. Every `git add` fails. I retried 4x, then REFUSED to force it: handbook 13 rule 4 forbids deleting the lock while a git process runs and I could not establish that none is -- ps -W / tasklist / Get-Process are ALL permission-blocked in this harness. I then tried the reversible move-aside (on Windows it fails if a live process holds the file, so success would itself have proven staleness) and the harness blocks .git/index.lock as a sensitive path. Correct guardrails, so I stopped instead of routing around them and filed BL-029 with the exact fileset + suggested commit message. THIS IS SPRINT-WIDE, NOT MY STORY: US-526/527/528/529 will all hit the same wall at step 6, so the next iteration should expect it. DO NOT SWITCH BRANCHES until it is cleared and the fileset is committed -- uncommitted work is precisely what handbook 13 says vanishes. Two dirty files are NOT ours: .deploy-version (PM/deploy artifact) and offices/uidevloper/proposals/... (Iris).

TD-059, SEVENTH SIGHTING, and the DANGEROUS variant: I booted into a tree where US-525 was already implemented with ralph_agents.json still showing me active on it. US-524's instance was at least COMMITTED; this one was not. Per the US-505 rule I re-ran the gate and VERIFIED rather than re-implementing. If you boot into a dirty tree matching your taskid, check `git log` AND `git status` before writing a line.

THE STORY'S REAL HEADLINE -- AC2 ANSWERED 'NOTHING REQUESTS THOSE ROUTES'. I-042's loudest evidence was a route auth anomaly (GET /boot, /shutdown = 401). The AC's own first job was to find what actually REQUESTS them before assuming the 401 was even on the render path -- and nothing does: splash-boot loads `/`, splash-grace loads `/shutdown.html`, dashboard loads `/dashboard.html`, all 200 with the token injected. Real, irrelevant, by-design. Chasing it would have eaten the story. Generalisable: when an issue ships with a striking piece of evidence, verify the evidence is ON the failure path before treating it as the cause.

THE ACTUAL DEFECT WAS A WRONG ANCHOR, NOT A SHORT DURATION (AC3). MIN_PLAY_MS=2500 already existed but was measured from SCRIPT PARSE, while the brand is an <object type=image/svg+xml> -- a separate ASYNC document that paints later. So the 'minimum play' window silently included the brand's own load time: on a cold chromium the splash met its own 2.5 s floor having shown the brand for a fraction of it, then faded. Grounded live (boot dc7a3848): splash-boot lived 9.806 s yet chromium burned the first ~5.4 s on startup -- the unit was NOT too short-lived. Fix re-anchors the SAME 2500 ms to the brand load event, so NO new magic number (Rule 2), pinned by a test that rejects any other floor value. TWO BOUNDS, both tested, both load-bearing: capped by HARD_CAP_MS so a slow asset cannot delay boot arbitrarily NOR tip a HEALTHY boot into the amber DEGRADED branch that persists until reboot; and brandReadyMs starts null (never 0) so a brand that NEVER loads falls back to the parse anchor. Miss that second bound and a missing splash.svg pins the splash until reboot -- the US-494 failure mode re-entered through its own fix. LESSON: when you add a WAIT to a boot path, the first question is what happens if the thing you wait for never arrives.

AC4 NEEDED NO CODE AND THE FINDING BEATS A PATCH: splash-grace already loads a served route. Nobody saw a reverse splash because the ONLY production writer of shutdown-state is the powerwatch ShutdownSequencer GRACE path -- a manual `sudo reboot` SIGTERMs eclipse-powerwatch without a grace sequence, so shutdown-state is never written and splash-grace.path never triggers. NO REVERSE SPLASH ON A BENCH REBOOT IS CORRECT. I-042's shutdown half was expected behaviour, not a regression. Anyone drilling the reverse splash needs a REAL AC-loss event.

AC5 held in the awkward direction: the test asserts bare routes STAY 401, specifically to stop a future fix from making them public to 'resolve I-042' (TD-067, Atlas BLOCK). _tokenOk untouched, no new routes. AC6: the route-contract test parses the URL out of all SIX real kiosk units (both session variants -- install.sh picks one, so a wayland-only regression would hide behind a green x11 test) and drives it against the REAL server over the REAL kits in the production assets-dir ORDER. Neither half can drift alone. It also asserts no __SPLASH_TOKEN__ placeholder survives: a 200 carrying an unsubstituted token renders and then 401s every poll = blank splash, green status code.

TWO ISSUES FILED, NOT PATCHED (both proven on the box, both out of scope). I-043: shutdown-state-poll.js funnels FOUR different terminal outcomes through one silent window.close(), so a correct abort and a race are indistinguishable from the journal. splash-grace has fired exactly ONCE in retention (Jul 28, 2.17 s -- very likely never painted) and which case fired cannot be determined. That matters because the drill needs a rare power-loss event and burning one currently yields no diagnosis. I did NOT force a paint to make it visible: painting when the state says the shutdown is over is a dishonest instrument, the opposite of the splash's purpose. I-044: every kiosk unit sets XDG_RUNTIME_DIR=/run/user/%U and %U expands to 0, NOT the User= UID -- `systemctl show` returns /run/user/0 while the real dir is /run/user/1000, producing dconf Permission-denied x3 + a dbus 'Could not parse server address' run in the journal. NOT the render cause (X11 needs only DISPLAY). Filed because the fix touches every kiosk template + install.sh = the deploy contract. Its own lesson: verify against `systemctl show -p Environment`, never against the unit TEXT -- this bug exists because %U looked right in the file.

GATE, SYNCHRONOUS, IN-LOOP: 2 new files = 28 passed, ZERO SKIPS (checked on purpose -- the floor tests skip without node and a silent skip would void the whole timing catalog, US-524's lesson). Then the FULL scoped suites because boot-state-poll.js + render_harness.py + splash_probe.js are shared by every splash/UI test: tests/ui + tests/pi/splash = 794 passed, 1 skipped (POSIX file-mode on Windows, pre-existing), 2 FAILED = I-041 = US-528 IN THIS SPRINT. I PROVED that provenance rather than asserting it (US-518 lesson): `git log` shows the production emitter last changed by US-505 (65de58d) while its exact-shape test last moved two stories earlier (f929ed8), and `git status` shows both files untouched in my tree. ruff clean on all 3 touched Python files. `make` is NOT on PATH -- `make lint` exits 127, which reads like a pass. TD-075 still stands, so lint was per-touched-file.

OWED, NOT FAKED: validationCriteria wants a Pi reboot (PM deploy, handbook 13). The boot half is now meaningfully observable -- expect the brand HELD ~2.5 s after it paints instead of fading mid-appearance. The shutdown half CANNOT be validated by a reboot at all per the AC4 finding, and until I-043 lands a real AC-loss drill will not tell you WHY if it fails.

NEXT UP is US-526 (production drain-event writer, M, the BL-028 carry-over) -- expect BL-029 to block its commit too. Its traps are already spelled out in the AC: read the UPS LATE-BOUND at transition time (the US-501/502/503/505 boot-order trap, now five sightings), and the boot reaper MUST NOT call endDrainEvent (it computes runtime_seconds from a timestamp delta, so across a reboot it would manufacture a multi-hour runtime) -- stamp end_timestamp only, leaving runtime_seconds AND end_vcell_v NULL.
